summary: Toolkit/Level Transform Guidance — a HUB for level-design tools, one tab per tool.
overview: Level-design tool for dressing and checking a level, featuring a Clipping Inspector, a Heatmap Grid, a Measuring Tape and Snap To Mouse. Four tabs in one window, sharing units, layer filtering and Scene-view drawing. It reports, it never fixes or grades — every tab surfaces information and leaves the call to you.

features.name: Clipping Inspector
features.what: scans the level for objects sunk into each other on chosen layers, and paints the buried part.

features.name: Heatmap Grid
features.what: colours a movable grid by how much stuff is in each cell, to find over-dressed and barren areas. Doubles as a ruler.

features.name: Measuring Tape
features.what: click points in the Scene view to measure real distances, labelled per segment.

features.name: Snap To Mouse
features.what: press a key to teleport the selected object onto whatever surface the mouse points at.

useCases: Checking nothing is sunk into the floor before art replaces greybox.
Finding the wing of a level that is under-dressed, or the cluster that is overloaded.
Confirming a doorway, corridor or jump gap is the width the design calls for.
Scattering props onto uneven terrain without hand-editing Y values.
Inspecting one storey of a stacked level in isolation.

walkthrough.name: Subjects (get painted)
walkthrough.what: Layers that get scanned and highlighted. Only these are painted.

walkthrough.name: Targets (clipped into)
walkthrough.what: Layers a subject may be buried in. Keeping floors here and out of Subjects is why architecture never lights up.

walkthrough.name: Mode
walkthrough.what: Collider checks what blocks the player; Mesh checks what you see. They disagree often.

walkthrough.name: Overlap Tolerance
walkthrough.what: How far things must interpenetrate to count. Raise it to stop normal resting contact being flagged.

walkthrough.name: Highlight Style
walkthrough.what: Buried Portion Only paints just the part inside other geometry, so you see how deep. Whole Object tints all of it.

walkthrough.name: Highlight Selection Live
walkthrough.what: Highlights as you select, without running a scan.

walkthrough.name: Scan Whole Level / Scan Selection
walkthrough.what: Runs the check. Results list has a Select button per row.

walkthrough.name: Region (Center / Size)
walkthrough.what: The box the grid covers, draggable in the Scene view. X and Z are the footprint; Y is a height slice, counting only objects whose centre is inside it.

walkthrough.name: Cell Size + Unit
walkthrough.what: Grid square size in your chosen unit. Round numbers make the grid readable as a ruler.

walkthrough.name: Metric
walkthrough.what: Bounds Volume for visual heaviness; Object Count for a plain tally.

walkthrough.name: Full Red At
walkthrough.what: The density that counts as fully red. A fixed scale you set, not auto-fitted to the busiest cell.

walkthrough.name: Counted Layers
walkthrough.what: Which layers contribute to a cell's value.

walkthrough.name: Drape Onto Floor + Floor Layers
walkthrough.what: Raycasts each cell down so the grid follows terrain instead of one flat plane.

walkthrough.name: Fill Opacity / Draw Through Geometry
walkthrough.what: Readability only — how strong the colour is, and whether it draws over occluding geometry.

walkthrough.name: Build / Refresh Grid
walkthrough.what: Rebuilds the grid. It is cached, so do this after moving things.

walkthrough.name: Measuring Enabled
walkthrough.what: Turns Scene-view click capture on and off.

walkthrough.name: Mode
walkthrough.what: 3D raycasts real colliders and rejects clicks that hit nothing. 2D projects onto a fixed world plane, for measuring across open space.

walkthrough.name: Fixed Plane
walkthrough.what: Which world plane 2D mode projects onto (Z, Y or X). Never the camera's view, so points hold as you orbit.

walkthrough.name: Unit
walkthrough.what: Display unit for distances. Shared with the Heatmap tab.

walkthrough.name: Label Style
walkthrough.what: Badge is legible on any background. Auto Contrast samples the surface colour and can guess wrong on textured art. Fixed Color is a colour you pick.

walkthrough.name: Clear Points
walkthrough.what: Removes all points. Middle-click in the Scene view does the same.

walkthrough.name: Surface Mask
walkthrough.what: Layers the object is allowed to land on.

walkthrough.name: Snap Key
walkthrough.what: Key to press while hovering the Scene view. Defaults to V. One press, one jump.

walkthrough.name: Align rotation to surface normal
walkthrough.what: Also rotates the object's up axis to match the surface, for props that should sit flush on a slope.

gotchas.title: It reports, it does not grade
gotchas.body: Nothing can tell whether an intersection was intended. An empty result list means 'nothing obvious at these settings', not 'the level is correct'.

gotchas.title: Only the active tab runs
gotchas.body: Switching tabs deactivates the old one; closing the window deactivates all four. A tab's Scene-view drawing disappears when you switch away — the data is still there, it just is not being drawn.

gotchas.title: Collider and Mesh modes will disagree
gotchas.body: A box collider can read as clean while the visual mesh clearly pokes through a wall, and the reverse. Pick the mode that matches the question.

gotchas.title: The grid is cached, not live
gotchas.body: It rebuilds on demand and when the hierarchy changes, never per frame. Moving objects does not recolour it — press Build / Refresh Grid.

gotchas.title: Full Red At changes the story
gotchas.body: Set it once for a level's scale and leave it, or two readings are not comparable. Too high and dense areas read as mild; too low and everything saturates.

gotchas.title: The height slice filters by centre
gotchas.body: A tall object whose centre sits above the slice is not counted, even though it passes through the area.

gotchas.title: 3D mode rejects clicks that miss geometry
gotchas.body: That is what guarantees every point is a real world position. Use 2D mode to measure across open space.

gotchas.title: It snaps the pivot, not the base
gotchas.body: A prop whose pivot is at its centre ends up half-buried. Prefabs for this want their pivot at the foot of the model.
